model: fixed inverse-variance weights derived from original individual errors; Cov(Y_i,Y_j)=rho*sigma_i*sigma_j for i!=j; var(mean)=var0+rho*(var1-var0); expected aperture=fraction*5.5; spectral prediction sigma=fraction*0.66; extra additive systematic independent; z=(expected-mean)/sqrt(var_mean+spectral_variance+extra_variance)
assumptions: The 5.5 nJy published model line-only synthetic photometry applies at the frozen sky position and is linearly proportional to the NIRSpec flux.
The fraction parameter is an ASSUMED effective net aperture fraction including sky-annulus subtraction; it is not measured encircled energy or PSF injection result.
rho is an ASSUMED nonnegative uniform cross-epoch noise correlation; it has not been measured from common blank-sky control positions.
The optional additive systematic in nJy is a stress parameter, not an estimated error budget.
NIRSpec and NIRCam uncertainties are treated as independent; line-flux calibration and potential spatial confusion are not fully modeled.
No photometric event timing or intrinsic variability is inferred from these scenarios alone.
next_experiment: Measure co-located aperture residual covariances across four original i2d mosaics with independent blank sky coordinates and PSF+annulus injection-recovery for 2023 epochs; then perform correctly calibrated NIRSpec extraction at 15850.793 and 13656.748 Å with stage-2 background, shutters, and wavelength-dependent throughput.
